title: Palatalization of TI, CI, SI before Vowels (/ʃ/, /ʒ/)
objectives: Identify palatalized coronal sequences TI, CI, SI before vowels

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: Palatalization of TI, CI, SI before Vowels (/ʃ/, /ʒ/). Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner says /s/ in "special".
💡 Solution: Show mouth position: tongue pulls back to palate making /ʃ/ sh sound.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Palatalization of TI, CI, SI before Vowels (/ʃ/, /ʒ/)
1. Definition: Coronal stops and fricatives (t, c, s) followed by i + vowel blend into postalveolar fricatives /ʃ/ or /ʒ/.

2. Rule: 1. ti + vowel = /ʃ/ (patient, partial, nation). 2. ci + vowel = /ʃ/ (special, social, official). 3. si + vowel after consonant = /ʃ/ (tension, mansion). 4. si + vowel after vowel = /ʒ/ (vision, occasion, decision).
3. Why? Historical palatalization: high vowel /i/ pulled the preceding tongue contact back to the hard palate.
4. How to recognize? Look for ti, ci, si followed immediately by a vowel letter.
5. Common examples: patient /ˈpeɪʃənt/, special /ˈspɛʃəl/, official /əˈfɪʃəl/, tension /ˈtɛnʃən/, vision /ˈvɪʒən/, occasion /əˈkeɪʒən/
6. Counter-examples: ti in question /s/ + /tʃ/ -> /ˈkwɛstʃən/ (after s, ti becomes /tʃ/).
7. Exceptions: satiety /səˈtaɪəti/ (stressed i prevents palatalization).
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing "patient" as *pa-ti-ent in three separate syllables.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: ti/ci = /ʃ/ (sh)! si after vowel = /ʒ/ (zh)!
10. Key vocabulary: palatalization, coronal stop, postalveolar fricative, assimilation, Latinate spelling
11. Frequency: ★★★★☆ (High)
12. CEFR Level: 🔵 B2
13. Associated Visual: 🌊 Wave showing tongue sliding back to palate for /ʃ/ and /ʒ/.
14. Key Takeaway: TI/CI/SI + vowel = /ʃ/ or /ʒ/! Never pronounce as separate T-I-E!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: How is "ti" pronounced in "patient"? (/ʃ/ sh sound)
CCQ 2: What is the difference between "sion" in "tension" and "vision"? (tension = voiceless /ʃ/ after consonant n; vision = voiced /ʒ/ after vowel i)
CCQ 3: Do you pronounce 3 separate syllables in "social"? (No, 2 syllables: /ˈsoʊ.ʃəl/)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Classify as voiceless /ʃ/ or voiced /ʒ/:
🎯 Item: patient ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Voiceless /ʃ/ (ti + vowel)
🎯 Item: vision ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Voiced /ʒ/ (si + vowel after vowel)
🎯 Item: tension ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Voiceless /ʃ/ (si + vowel after consonant)
